previous_disclosures.summary: The company identifies four reportable business units: Compute and Networking (CNBU), Mobile (MBU), Embedded (EBU), and Storage (SBU), each comprising specific memory, storage, and networking products for defined markets.

current_disclosures.summary: Segment information is consistent with how it is reviewed and evaluated by the chief operating decision maker, with four reportable business units identified.
The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
The Mobile Business Unit includes memory and storage products sold into the smartphone and other mobile-device markets.
The Embedded Business Unit includes memory and storage products and solutions sold into the intelligent edge through the automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets.
The Storage Business Unit includes SSDs and component-level storage solutions sold into the data center, PC, and consumer markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose their reportable business units or segments and list specific product categories served. MU's CNBU focuses on memory products for data center, PC, graphics, and networking. AMD's segments include Data Center (AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs), Client (CPUs, APUs for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs), and Embedded. While MU emphasizes memory solutions across these end markets, AMD structures its reporting around distinct silicon types (CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators) with specific end-market mappings like Client for desktops/notebooks and Gaming for discrete GPUs.

sentences.text: Compute and Networking Business Unit ("CNBU"): Includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
The Company's four reportable segments are:

• the Data Center segment, which primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers;
• the Client segment, which primarily includes CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks;
• the Gaming segment, which primarily includes discrete GPUs, and semi-custom SoC products and development services; and
• the Embedded segment, which primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, System on Modules (SOMs), and Adaptive SoC products.

comparisons.peer_summary: The semiconductor solutions segment provides devices for data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking, as well as products for mobile, set-top box, broadband access, storage, industrial, and automotive markets. The segment also includes IP licensing.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO identify specific market applications for their semiconductor solutions, with significant overlap in the data center and networking sectors. MU's CNBU includes memory products sold into the data center and networking markets. AVGO's Semiconductor Solutions segment provides devices for data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking. AVGO also explicitly mentions set-top box and broadband access markets, which are distinct from MU's defined PC, graphics, and embedded focuses.

sentences.text: Compute and Networking Business Unit ("CNBU"): Includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
We provide semiconductor solutions for managing the movement of data in data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking and connectivity.

We also provide semiconductor solutions for enabling the set-top box and broadband access markets and for enabling secure movement of digital data to and from host machines, such as servers, personal computers and storage systems, to the underlying storage devices, such as hard disk drives and solid state drives.

comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose their reportable segment structure. MU identifies the Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU) as including memory products for data center and networking. INTC organizes its business into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All Other, with Data Center and AI (DCAI) and Network and Edge (NEX) being key components within Intel Products. INTC provides a more granular breakdown of operating segments (CCG, DCAI, NEX) compared to MU's broader CNBU definition, though both cover data center and networking markets.
